A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPTI research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-synthesis experiments, including FID comparisons across six datasets and image-voting and model-backend ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original synthesis experiments and adds CelebA classification results, bird-dataset experiments, and further model-backend results.

M1.justification: The central SPTI pipeline is retained. Algorithm 2 makes limited computational corrections: lookahead variations take the current caption population instead of N, embeddings are averaged without the extra Phi operation, and population expansion uses L-1 instead of K-1. These establish corrections to the specified algorithm, without establishing an implementation change.

E1.justification: The original six synthesis datasets remain. v3 adds CelebA Wearing_Lipstick classification, extending evaluation to downstream predictive utility, and ImageNet100-derived bird populations with different class diversity in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DP-finetune comparisons on LSUN Bedroom, Cat, European Art, Wave-ui-25k, and Sprite Fright; v1 compares only SPTI and PE there, although DP-finetune already appears on MM-CelebA-HQ. The new classification evaluation also includes a classifier trained on real data as a reference alongside PE-generated data.

E3.justification: The new downstream protocol trains WRN-40-4 on 2,000–10,000 synthetic or real samples and evaluates classification accuracy. Appendix D introduces a controlled design crossing two versus twenty bird classes with 200 versus 2,000 images. For retained Cat experiments, the reported lookahead degree changes from 8 to 4 for both SPTI and PE; this does not itself establish rerunning.

E4.justification: New Appendix D investigates whether the Cat failure reflects limited diversity or small dataset size through controlled bird experiments. Appendix B.3 adds training/test learning curves and comparative generated-face examples. The retained API-choice ablation also gains an Infinity backend in Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for the empirical results. Added training curves and experimental conditions do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerous FID values and trajectories are revised. At epsilon=1, Table 1 changes LSUN Bedroom from 26.71 to 26.39 and European Art from 50.78 to 57.64. Table 2 reverses the SPTI backbone ranking: LDM versus SDXL changes from 37.96 versus 33.27 to 33.41 versus 34.17. New baseline, classification, bird, and Infinity results substantially expand the evidence. Cat changes cannot be treated as same-setting gains because its reported lookahead changes.

T1.justification: The formal DP definition, Wasserstein formulation, histogram-sensitivity argument, Gaussian calibration and composition equation, and postprocessing guarantee are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive revision to the privacy reasoning appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free, API-compatible DP image synthesis through textual intermediaries and image-space voting. The new evaluations support these existing contributions rather than redefine them. Changing headline FID inequalities to equalities does not alter the central scientific claim.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes poor Cat/bird performance to low diversity rather than small sample size alone, adding a substantive applicability boundary. Section 4.3 links downstream gains to synthetic-data diversity. Section 7 explicitly acknowledges higher computational demands than PE and argues that diversity and generalization benefits justify the cost.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-release link and substantially expands resource disclosures. Section 7 replaces the brief 80 GB hardware statement with approximately 70 GB peak memory, 19 hours on an A800 or 15.5 hours on two A100s, PE resource comparisons, and token budgets. It also documents the new classifier and bird-subset construction; most existing hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kong and Syed's concurrent caption-based private photo-album synthesis and explicitly distinguishes its hierarchical fine-tuning from SPTI's API-based image voting. It also adds a Struct-Bench citation. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. v3 inserts a downstream-task subsection and new appendix analyses, expands the computational-overhead discussion, and makes local wording, citation, affiliation, and venue edits. Existing configuration and dataset appendices move from D/E to E/F.

P2.justification: Figure 1 redraws the SPTI flow to show private images as references for evolving random captions. Appendix FID plots are redrawn and reorganized into paired layouts. v3 adds classification and learning-curve figures, comparative face panels, and the bird-results table, while expanding Table 1 with baseline rows and Table 4 with an Infinity column.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily validated utility through FID and left the Cat failure unexplained. v3 adds direct downstream-utility evidence, a controlled diversity-versus-size investigation, broader DP-finetuning comparisons, and explicit computational costs, substantially improving empirical support and applicability assessment. Reporting consistency weakens because the abstract retains the earlier 26.71/33.27 headline values despite revised Tables 1–2. That defect limits numerical clarity but does not outweigh the substantive gains in validation and limitations analysis.
